newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PLANS TO MARK JACKIE ROBINSON ANNIVERSARY IN PLACE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PLANS TO MARK JACKIE ROBINSON ANNIVERSARY IN PLACE.

text.p: Major League Baseball is dedicating this season in honour of the 50th anniversary of Jackie Robinson's debut with the Brooklyn Dodgers that broke baseball's colour barrier and President Clinton will join the celebration.

Robinson, a Hall of Fame second baseman, broke the colour line on April 15, 1947 in a game between the Dodgers and Boston Braves at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn. A ceremony is planned during this season's April 15 game between the New York Mets and the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers.

"Yesterday we learned that the president (Bill Clinton) will join in the celebration by attending the game," said acting commissioner Bud Selig. "That special game will be stopped in the middle innings for a special presentation."
Clinton will join Rachel Robinson, Jackie's widow, at second base during a fifth-inning ceremony, Selig said.
"Fifty years ago, Jackie Robinson and Major League Baseball together made history and forever moved the United States to a higher level of equality," Selig told a news conference.
"We are honoured to join with the (Jackie Robinson) Foundation in celebrating Jackie's legacy during the anniversary year."
The Jackie Robinson Foundation was established by Rachel Robinson in 1973 to help needy black students gain college scholarships.
National League president Leonard Coleman, an African American who also serves as chairman of the foundation, paid tribute to Robinson.
"I remember Jackie dancing off first base as a kid growing up. When he danced off the base he was not only shaking up the pitcher, but our society as a whole," said Coleman.

American League president Gene Budig said: "Jackie Robinson led America by example. He reminded people about what was right and what was wrong. I think we can clearly say that Jackie Robinson made America a better place then and now."
Robinson, the first black man to play in any of the major U.S. professional team sports, played 10 seasons with the Dodgers, before retiring after the 1956 season.
He was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1962 and died 10 years later at age 53 from a heart attack brought about by chronic diabetes.
Baseball's initiatives include the wearing of commemorative patches on the uniforms of major and minor league players and umpires throughout the season.

Fund-raising activities will be conducted to benefit the foundation's scholarship programmes. Additional cross-licensing and sponsorship activities will be conducted by Major League Baseball, its teams and the foundation.

Major League Baseball also announced that Larry Doby, who broke the colour barrier in the American League with the Cleveland Indians, will be honoured during the All-Star Game on July 8 in Cleveland and will be honorary captain of the Amercian League team.
